links.passage: Science- and technology-based irrigation scheduling approaches, as opposed to the Checkbook method or the condition of crop method, may boost crop profit while reducing environmental consequences by limiting crop water stress (Zhang et al., 2021).

Examples of such applications include an irrigation system developed by Glória et al. (2021) to attain the best water-saving schedule using real-time data, and smart irrigation strategies that predict irrigation water use using several ML algorithms (see Tace et al., 2022).

The application of ML in irrigation scheduling promoted agricultural productivity and water use efficiency (Hunsaker et al., 2005; Karasekreter et al., 2013; Nachankar et al., 2018; Nawandar and Satpute, 2019; Jamroen et al., 2020; Jimenez et al., 2020).
